13 /-!
14 # Angles between points
15 
16 This file defines unoriented angles in Euclidean affine spaces.
17 
18 ## Main definitions
19 
20 * `EuclideanGeometry.angle`, with notation `∠`, is the undirected angle determined by three
21   points.
22 -/

35 variable {V P : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup V] [InnerProductSpace ℝ V] [MetricSpace P]
36   [NormedAddTorsor V P] {p p₀ : P}
37 
38 /-- The undirected angle at `p₂` between the line segments to `p₁` and
39 `p₃`. If either of those points equals `p₂`, this is π/2. Use
40 `open scoped EuclideanGeometry` to access the `∠ p₁ p₂ p₃`
41 notation. -/
42 nonrec def angle (p₁ p₂ p₃ : P) : ℝ :=
43   angle (p₁ -ᵥ p₂ : V) (p₃ -ᵥ p₂)
44 
45 @[inherit_doc] scoped notation "∠" => EuclideanGeometry.angle
46 
47 theorem continuousAt_angle {x : P × P × P} (hx12 : x.1 ≠ x.2.1) (hx32 : x.2.2 ≠ x.2.1) :
48     ContinuousAt (fun y : P × P × P => ∠ y.1 y.2.1 y.2.2) x := by
49   let f : P × P × P → V × V := fun y => (y.1 -ᵥ y.2.1, y.2.2 -ᵥ y.2.1)
50   have hf1 : (f x).1 ≠ 0 := by simp [f, hx12]
51   have hf2 : (f x).2 ≠ 0 := by simp [f, hx32]
52   exact (InnerProductGeometry.continuousAt_angle hf1 hf2).comp (by fun_prop)
53 
54 @[simp]
55 theorem _root_.AffineIsometry.angle_map {V₂ P₂ : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup V₂]
56     [InnerProductSpace ℝ V₂] [MetricSpace P₂] [NormedAddTorsor V₂ P₂]
57     (f : P →ᵃⁱ[ℝ] P₂) (p₁ p₂ p₃ : P) : ∠ (f p₁) (f p₂) (f p₃) = ∠ p₁ p₂ p₃ := by
58   simp_rw [angle, ← AffineIsometry.map_vsub, LinearIsometry.angle_map]
59 
60 @[simp, norm_cast]
61 theorem _root_.AffineSubspace.angle_coe {s : AffineSubspace ℝ P} (p₁ p₂ p₃ : s) :
62     haveI : Nonempty s := ⟨p₁⟩
63     ∠ (p₁ : P) (p₂ : P) (p₃ : P) = ∠ p₁ p₂ p₃ :=
64   haveI : Nonempty s := ⟨p₁⟩
65   s.subtypeₐᵢ.angle_map p₁ p₂ p₃

67 /-- A homothety with a nonzero scale factor preserves angles. -/
68 @[simp] lemma angle_homothety (p p₁ p₂ p₃ : P) {r : ℝ} (h : r ≠ 0) :
69     ∠ (AffineMap.homothety p r p₁) (AffineMap.homothety p r p₂) (AffineMap.homothety p r p₃) =
70       ∠ p₁ p₂ p₃ := by
71   simp_rw [angle, ← AffineMap.linearMap_vsub, AffineMap.homothety_linear, LinearMap.smul_apply,
72     LinearMap.id_coe, id_eq]
73   rcases h.lt_or_gt with hlt | hlt <;> simp [hlt, -neg_vsub_eq_vsub_rev]
74 
75 /-- Angles are translation invariant. -/
76 @[simp]
77 theorem angle_const_vadd (v : V) (p₁ p₂ p₃ : P) : ∠ (v +ᵥ p₁) (v +ᵥ p₂) (v +ᵥ p₃) = ∠ p₁ p₂ p₃ :=
78   (AffineIsometryEquiv.constVAdd ℝ P v).toAffineIsometry.angle_map _ _ _
79 
80 /-- Angles are translation invariant. -/
81 @[simp]
82 theorem angle_vadd_const (v₁ v₂ v₃ : V) (p : P) : ∠ (v₁ +ᵥ p) (v₂ +ᵥ p) (v₃ +ᵥ p) = ∠ v₁ v₂ v₃ :=
83   (AffineIsometryEquiv.vaddConst ℝ p).toAffineIsometry.angle_map _ _ _
84 
85 /-- Angles are translation invariant. -/
86 @[simp]
87 theorem angle_const_vsub (p p₁ p₂ p₃ : P) : ∠ (p -ᵥ p₁) (p -ᵥ p₂) (p -ᵥ p₃) = ∠ p₁ p₂ p₃ :=
88   (AffineIsometryEquiv.constVSub ℝ p).toAffineIsometry.angle_map _ _ _
89 
90 /-- Angles are translation invariant. -/
91 @[simp]
92 theorem angle_vsub_const (p₁ p₂ p₃ p : P) : ∠ (p₁ -ᵥ p) (p₂ -ᵥ p) (p₃ -ᵥ p) = ∠ p₁ p₂ p₃ :=
93   (AffineIsometryEquiv.vaddConst ℝ p).symm.toAffineIsometry.angle_map _ _ _
94 
95 /-- Angles in a vector space are translation invariant. -/
96 @[simp]
97 theorem angle_add_const (v₁ v₂ v₃ : V) (v : V) : ∠ (v₁ + v) (v₂ + v) (v₃ + v) = ∠ v₁ v₂ v₃ :=
98   angle_vadd_const _ _ _ _
99 
100 /-- Angles in a vector space are translation invariant. -/
101 @[simp]
102 theorem angle_const_add (v : V) (v₁ v₂ v₃ : V) : ∠ (v + v₁) (v + v₂) (v + v₃) = ∠ v₁ v₂ v₃ :=
103   angle_const_vadd _ _ _ _
104 
105 /-- Angles in a vector space are translation invariant. -/
106 @[simp]
107 theorem angle_sub_const (v₁ v₂ v₃ : V) (v : V) : ∠ (v₁ - v) (v₂ - v) (v₃ - v) = ∠ v₁ v₂ v₃ := by
108   simpa only [vsub_eq_sub] using angle_vsub_const v₁ v₂ v₃ v
109 
110 /-- Angles in a vector space are invariant under inversion. -/
111 @[simp]
112 theorem angle_const_sub (v : V) (v₁ v₂ v₃ : V) : ∠ (v - v₁) (v - v₂) (v - v₃) = ∠ v₁ v₂ v₃ := by
113   simpa only [vsub_eq_sub] using angle_const_vsub v v₁ v₂ v₃
114 
115 /-- Angles in a vector space are invariant under inversion. -/
116 @[simp]
117 theorem angle_neg (v₁ v₂ v₃ : V) : ∠ (-v₁) (-v₂) (-v₃) = ∠ v₁ v₂ v₃ := by
118   simpa only [zero_sub] using angle_const_sub 0 v₁ v₂ v₃
119 
120 /-- The angle at a point does not depend on the order of the other two
121 points. -/
122 nonrec theorem angle_comm (p₁ p₂ p₃ : P) : ∠ p₁ p₂ p₃ = ∠ p₃ p₂ p₁ :=
123   angle_comm _ _
124 
125 /-- The angle at a point is nonnegative. -/
126 nonrec theorem angle_nonneg (p₁ p₂ p₃ : P) : 0 ≤ ∠ p₁ p₂ p₃ :=
127   angle_nonneg _ _
128 
129 /-- The angle at a point is at most π. -/
130 nonrec theorem angle_le_pi (p₁ p₂ p₃ : P) : ∠ p₁ p₂ p₃ ≤ π :=
131   angle_le_pi _ _
132 
133 /-- The angle ∠AAB at a point is always `π / 2`. -/
134 @[simp] lemma angle_self_left (p₀ p : P) : ∠ p₀ p₀ p = π / 2 := by
135   unfold angle
136   rw [vsub_self]
137   exact angle_zero_left _
138 
139 /-- The angle ∠ABB at a point is always `π / 2`. -/
140 @[simp] lemma angle_self_right (p₀ p : P) : ∠ p p₀ p₀ = π / 2 := by rw [angle_comm, angle_self_left]
141 
142 /-- The angle ∠ABA at a point is `0`, unless `A = B`. -/
143 theorem angle_self_of_ne (h : p ≠ p₀) : ∠ p p₀ p = 0 := angle_self <| vsub_ne_zero.2 h
144 
145 
146 /-- If the angle ∠ABC at a point is π, the angle ∠BAC is 0. -/
147 theorem angle_eq_zero_of_angle_eq_pi_left {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} (h : ∠ p₁ p₂ p₃ = π) : ∠ p₂ p₁ p₃ = 0 := by
148   unfold angle at h
149   rw [angle_eq_pi_iff] at h
150   rcases h with ⟨hp₁p₂, ⟨r, ⟨hr, hpr⟩⟩⟩
151   unfold angle
152   rw [angle_eq_zero_iff]
153   rw [← neg_vsub_eq_vsub_rev, neg_ne_zero] at hp₁p₂
154   use hp₁p₂, -r + 1, add_pos (neg_pos_of_neg hr) zero_lt_one
155   rw [add_smul, ← neg_vsub_eq_vsub_rev p₁ p₂, smul_neg]
156   simp [← hpr]
157 
158 /-- If the angle ∠ABC at a point is π, the angle ∠BCA is 0. -/
159 theorem angle_eq_zero_of_angle_eq_pi_right {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} (h : ∠ p₁ p₂ p₃ = π) :
160     ∠ p₂ p₃ p₁ = 0 := by
161   rw [angle_comm] at h
162   exact angle_eq_zero_of_angle_eq_pi_left h
163 
164 /-- If ∠BCD = π, then ∠ABC = ∠ABD. -/
165 theorem angle_eq_angle_of_angle_eq_pi (p₁ : P) {p₂ p₃ p₄ : P} (h : ∠ p₂ p₃ p₄ = π) :
166     ∠ p₁ p₂ p₃ = ∠ p₁ p₂ p₄ := by
167   unfold angle at *
168   rcases angle_eq_pi_iff.1 h with ⟨_, ⟨r, ⟨hr, hpr⟩⟩⟩
169   rw [eq_comm]
170   convert angle_smul_right_of_pos (p₁ -ᵥ p₂) (p₃ -ᵥ p₂) (add_pos (neg_pos_of_neg hr) zero_lt_one)
171   rw [add_smul, ← neg_vsub_eq_vsub_rev p₂ p₃, smul_neg, neg_smul, ← hpr]
172   simp
173 
174 /-- If ∠BCD = π, then ∠ACB + ∠ACD = π. -/
175 nonrec theorem angle_add_angle_eq_pi_of_angle_eq_pi (p₁ : P) {p₂ p₃ p₄ : P} (h : ∠ p₂ p₃ p₄ = π) :
176     ∠ p₁ p₃ p₂ + ∠ p₁ p₃ p₄ = π := by
177   unfold angle at h
178   rw [angle_comm p₁ p₃ p₂, angle_comm p₁ p₃ p₄]
179   unfold angle
180   exact angle_add_angle_eq_pi_of_angle_eq_pi _ h
181 
182 /-- **Vertical Angles Theorem**: angles opposite each other, formed by two intersecting straight
183 lines, are equal. -/
184 theorem angle_eq_angle_of_angle_eq_pi_of_angle_eq_pi {p₁ p₂ p₃ p₄ p₅ : P} (hapc : ∠ p₁ p₅ p₃ = π)
185     (hbpd : ∠ p₂ p₅ p₄ = π) : ∠ p₁ p₅ p₂ = ∠ p₃ p₅ p₄ := by
186   linarith [angle_add_angle_eq_pi_of_angle_eq_pi p₁ hbpd, angle_comm p₄ p₅ p₁,
187     angle_add_angle_eq_pi_of_angle_eq_pi p₄ hapc, angle_comm p₄ p₅ p₃]
188 
189 /-- If ∠ABC = π then dist A B ≠ 0. -/
190 theorem left_dist_ne_zero_of_angle_eq_pi {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} (h : ∠ p₁ p₂ p₃ = π) : dist p₁ p₂ ≠ 0 := by
191   by_contra heq
192   rw [dist_eq_zero] at heq
193   rw [heq, angle_self_left] at h
194   exact Real.pi_ne_zero (by linarith)
195 
196 /-- If ∠ABC = π then dist C B ≠ 0. -/
197 theorem right_dist_ne_zero_of_angle_eq_pi {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} (h : ∠ p₁ p₂ p₃ = π) : dist p₃ p₂ ≠ 0 :=
198   left_dist_ne_zero_of_angle_eq_pi <| (angle_comm _ _ _).trans h
199 
200 /-- If ∠ABC = π, then (dist A C) = (dist A B) + (dist B C). -/
201 theorem dist_eq_add_dist_of_angle_eq_pi {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} (h : ∠ p₁ p₂ p₃ = π) :
202     dist p₁ p₃ = dist p₁ p₂ + dist p₃ p₂ := by
203   rw [dist_eq_norm_vsub V, dist_eq_norm_vsub V, dist_eq_norm_vsub V, ← vsub_sub_vsub_cancel_right]
204   exact norm_sub_eq_add_norm_of_angle_eq_pi h
205 
206 /-- If A ≠ B and C ≠ B then ∠ABC = π if and only if (dist A C) = (dist A B) + (dist B C). -/
207 theorem dist_eq_add_dist_iff_angle_eq_pi {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} (hp₁p₂ : p₁ ≠ p₂) (hp₃p₂ : p₃ ≠ p₂) :
208     dist p₁ p₃ = dist p₁ p₂ + dist p₃ p₂ ↔ ∠ p₁ p₂ p₃ = π := by
209   rw [dist_eq_norm_vsub V, dist_eq_norm_vsub V, dist_eq_norm_vsub V, ← vsub_sub_vsub_cancel_right]
210   exact
211     norm_sub_eq_add_norm_iff_angle_eq_pi (fun he => hp₁p₂ (vsub_eq_zero_iff_eq.1 he)) fun he =>
212       hp₃p₂ (vsub_eq_zero_iff_eq.1 he)
213 
214 /-- If ∠ABC = 0, then (dist A C) = abs ((dist A B) - (dist B C)). -/
215 theorem dist_eq_abs_sub_dist_of_angle_eq_zero {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} (h : ∠ p₁ p₂ p₃ = 0) :
216     dist p₁ p₃ = |dist p₁ p₂ - dist p₃ p₂| := by
217   rw [dist_eq_norm_vsub V, dist_eq_norm_vsub V, dist_eq_norm_vsub V, ← vsub_sub_vsub_cancel_right]
218   exact norm_sub_eq_abs_sub_norm_of_angle_eq_zero h
219 
220 /-- If A ≠ B and C ≠ B then ∠ABC = 0 if and only if (dist A C) = abs ((dist A B) - (dist B C)). -/
221 theorem dist_eq_abs_sub_dist_iff_angle_eq_zero {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} (hp₁p₂ : p₁ ≠ p₂) (hp₃p₂ : p₃ ≠ p₂) :
222     dist p₁ p₃ = |dist p₁ p₂ - dist p₃ p₂| ↔ ∠ p₁ p₂ p₃ = 0 := by
223   rw [dist_eq_norm_vsub V, dist_eq_norm_vsub V, dist_eq_norm_vsub V, ← vsub_sub_vsub_cancel_right]
224   exact
225     norm_sub_eq_abs_sub_norm_iff_angle_eq_zero (fun he => hp₁p₂ (vsub_eq_zero_iff_eq.1 he))
226       fun he => hp₃p₂ (vsub_eq_zero_iff_eq.1 he)
227 
228 /-- If M is the midpoint of the segment AB, then ∠AMB = π. -/
229 theorem angle_midpoint_eq_pi (p₁ p₂ : P) (hp₁p₂ : p₁ ≠ p₂) : ∠ p₁ (midpoint ℝ p₁ p₂) p₂ = π := by
230   simp only [angle, left_vsub_midpoint, invOf_eq_inv, right_vsub_midpoint, inv_pos, zero_lt_two,
231     angle_smul_right_of_pos, angle_smul_left_of_pos]
232   rw [← neg_vsub_eq_vsub_rev p₁ p₂]
233   apply angle_self_neg_of_nonzero
234   simpa only [ne_eq, vsub_eq_zero_iff_eq]
235 
236 /-- If M is the midpoint of the segment AB and C is the same distance from A as it is from B
237 then ∠CMA = π / 2. -/
238 theorem angle_left_midpoint_eq_pi_div_two_of_dist_eq {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} (h : dist p₃ p₁ = dist p₃ p₂) :
239     ∠ p₃ (midpoint ℝ p₁ p₂) p₁ = π / 2 := by
240   let m : P := midpoint ℝ p₁ p₂
241   have h1 : p₃ -ᵥ p₁ = p₃ -ᵥ m - (p₁ -ᵥ m) := (vsub_sub_vsub_cancel_right p₃ p₁ m).symm
242   have h2 : p₃ -ᵥ p₂ = p₃ -ᵥ m + (p₁ -ᵥ m) := by
243     rw [left_vsub_midpoint, ← midpoint_vsub_right, vsub_add_vsub_cancel]
244   rw [dist_eq_norm_vsub V p₃ p₁, dist_eq_norm_vsub V p₃ p₂, h1, h2] at h
245   exact (norm_add_eq_norm_sub_iff_angle_eq_pi_div_two (p₃ -ᵥ m) (p₁ -ᵥ m)).mp h.symm
246 
247 /-- If M is the midpoint of the segment AB and C is the same distance from A as it is from B
248 then ∠CMB = π / 2. -/
249 theorem angle_right_midpoint_eq_pi_div_two_of_dist_eq {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} (h : dist p₃ p₁ = dist p₃ p₂) :
250     ∠ p₃ (midpoint ℝ p₁ p₂) p₂ = π / 2 := by
251   rw [midpoint_comm p₁ p₂, angle_left_midpoint_eq_pi_div_two_of_dist_eq h.symm]
252 
253 /-- If the second of three points is strictly between the other two, the angle at that point
254 is π. -/
255 theorem _root_.Sbtw.angle₁₂₃_eq_pi {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} (h : Sbtw ℝ p₁ p₂ p₃) : ∠ p₁ p₂ p₃ = π := by
256   rw [angle, angle_eq_pi_iff]
257   rcases h with ⟨⟨r, ⟨hr0, hr1⟩, hp₂⟩, hp₂p₁, hp₂p₃⟩
258   refine ⟨vsub_ne_zero.2 hp₂p₁.symm, -(1 - r) / r, ?_⟩
259   have hr0' : r ≠ 0 := by
260     rintro rfl
261     rw [← hp₂] at hp₂p₁
262     simp at hp₂p₁
263   have hr1' : r ≠ 1 := by
264     rintro rfl
265     rw [← hp₂] at hp₂p₃
266     simp at hp₂p₃
267   replace hr0 := hr0.lt_of_ne hr0'.symm
268   replace hr1 := hr1.lt_of_ne hr1'
269   refine ⟨div_neg_of_neg_of_pos (Left.neg_neg_iff.2 (sub_pos.2 hr1)) hr0, ?_⟩
270   rw [← hp₂, AffineMap.lineMap_apply, vsub_vadd_eq_vsub_sub, vsub_vadd_eq_vsub_sub, vsub_self,
271     zero_sub, smul_neg, smul_smul, div_mul_cancel₀ _ hr0', neg_smul, neg_neg, sub_eq_iff_eq_add, ←
272     add_smul, sub_add_cancel, one_smul]
273 
274 /-- If the second of three points is strictly between the other two, the angle at that point
275 (reversed) is π. -/
276 theorem _root_.Sbtw.angle₃₂₁_eq_pi {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} (h : Sbtw ℝ p₁ p₂ p₃) : ∠ p₃ p₂ p₁ = π := by
277   rw [← h.angle₁₂₃_eq_pi, angle_comm]
278 
279 /-- The angle between three points is π if and only if the second point is strictly between the
280 other two. -/
281 theorem angle_eq_pi_iff_sbtw {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} : ∠ p₁ p₂ p₃ = π ↔ Sbtw ℝ p₁ p₂ p₃ := by
282   refine ⟨?_, fun h => h.angle₁₂₃_eq_pi⟩
283   rw [angle, angle_eq_pi_iff]
284   rintro ⟨hp₁p₂, r, hr, hp₃p₂⟩
285   refine ⟨⟨1 / (1 - r), ⟨div_nonneg zero_le_one (sub_nonneg.2 (hr.le.trans zero_le_one)),
286     (div_le_one (sub_pos.2 (hr.trans zero_lt_one))).2 ((le_sub_self_iff 1).2 hr.le)⟩, ?_⟩,
287     (vsub_ne_zero.1 hp₁p₂).symm, ?_⟩
288   · rw [← eq_vadd_iff_vsub_eq] at hp₃p₂
289     rw [AffineMap.lineMap_apply, hp₃p₂, vadd_vsub_assoc, ← neg_vsub_eq_vsub_rev p₂ p₁, smul_neg, ←
290       neg_smul, smul_add, smul_smul, ← add_smul, eq_comm, eq_vadd_iff_vsub_eq]
291     convert (one_smul ℝ (p₂ -ᵥ p₁)).symm
292     field [(sub_pos.2 (hr.trans zero_lt_one)).ne.symm]
293   · rw [ne_comm, ← @vsub_ne_zero V, hp₃p₂, smul_ne_zero_iff]
294     exact ⟨hr.ne, hp₁p₂⟩
295 
296 /-- If the second of three points is weakly between the other two, and not equal to the first,
297 the angle at the first point is zero. -/
298 theorem _root_.Wbtw.angle₂₁₃_eq_zero_of_ne {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} (h : Wbtw ℝ p₁ p₂ p₃) (hp₂p₁ : p₂ ≠ p₁) :
299     ∠ p₂ p₁ p₃ = 0 := by
300   rw [angle, angle_eq_zero_iff]
301   rcases h with ⟨r, ⟨hr0, hr1⟩, rfl⟩
302   have hr0' : r ≠ 0 := by
303     rintro rfl
304     simp at hp₂p₁
305   replace hr0 := hr0.lt_of_ne hr0'.symm
306   refine ⟨vsub_ne_zero.2 hp₂p₁, r⁻¹, inv_pos.2 hr0, ?_⟩
307   rw [AffineMap.lineMap_apply, vadd_vsub_assoc, vsub_self, add_zero, smul_smul,
308     inv_mul_cancel₀ hr0', one_smul]
309 
310 /-- If the second of three points is strictly between the other two, the angle at the first point
311 is zero. -/
312 theorem _root_.Sbtw.angle₂₁₃_eq_zero {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} (h : Sbtw ℝ p₁ p₂ p₃) : ∠ p₂ p₁ p₃ = 0 :=
313   h.wbtw.angle₂₁₃_eq_zero_of_ne h.ne_left
314 
315 /-- If the second of three points is weakly between the other two, and not equal to the first,
316 the angle at the first point (reversed) is zero. -/
317 theorem _root_.Wbtw.angle₃₁₂_eq_zero_of_ne {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} (h : Wbtw ℝ p₁ p₂ p₃) (hp₂p₁ : p₂ ≠ p₁) :
318     ∠ p₃ p₁ p₂ = 0 := by rw [← h.angle₂₁₃_eq_zero_of_ne hp₂p₁, angle_comm]
319 
320 /-- If the second of three points is strictly between the other two, the angle at the first point
321 (reversed) is zero. -/
322 theorem _root_.Sbtw.angle₃₁₂_eq_zero {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} (h : Sbtw ℝ p₁ p₂ p₃) : ∠ p₃ p₁ p₂ = 0 :=
323   h.wbtw.angle₃₁₂_eq_zero_of_ne h.ne_left
324 
325 /-- If the second of three points is weakly between the other two, and not equal to the third,
326 the angle at the third point is zero. -/
327 theorem _root_.Wbtw.angle₂₃₁_eq_zero_of_ne {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} (h : Wbtw ℝ p₁ p₂ p₃) (hp₂p₃ : p₂ ≠ p₃) :
328     ∠ p₂ p₃ p₁ = 0 :=
329   h.symm.angle₂₁₃_eq_zero_of_ne hp₂p₃
330 
331 /-- If the second of three points is strictly between the other two, the angle at the third point
332 is zero. -/
333 theorem _root_.Sbtw.angle₂₃₁_eq_zero {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} (h : Sbtw ℝ p₁ p₂ p₃) : ∠ p₂ p₃ p₁ = 0 :=
334   h.wbtw.angle₂₃₁_eq_zero_of_ne h.ne_right
335 
336 /-- If the second of three points is weakly between the other two, and not equal to the third,
337 the angle at the third point (reversed) is zero. -/
338 theorem _root_.Wbtw.angle₁₃₂_eq_zero_of_ne {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} (h : Wbtw ℝ p₁ p₂ p₃) (hp₂p₃ : p₂ ≠ p₃) :
339     ∠ p₁ p₃ p₂ = 0 :=
340   h.symm.angle₃₁₂_eq_zero_of_ne hp₂p₃
341 
342 /-- If the second of three points is strictly between the other two, the angle at the third point
343 (reversed) is zero. -/
344 theorem _root_.Sbtw.angle₁₃₂_eq_zero {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} (h : Sbtw ℝ p₁ p₂ p₃) : ∠ p₁ p₃ p₂ = 0 :=
345   h.wbtw.angle₁₃₂_eq_zero_of_ne h.ne_right
346 
347 /-- The angle between three points is zero if and only if one of the first and third points is
348 weakly between the other two, and not equal to the second. -/
349 theorem angle_eq_zero_iff_ne_and_wbtw {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} :
350     ∠ p₁ p₂ p₃ = 0 ↔ p₁ ≠ p₂ ∧ Wbtw ℝ p₂ p₁ p₃ ∨ p₃ ≠ p₂ ∧ Wbtw ℝ p₂ p₃ p₁ := by
351   constructor
352   · rw [angle, angle_eq_zero_iff]
353     rintro ⟨hp₁p₂, r, hr0, hp₃p₂⟩
354     rcases le_or_gt 1 r with (hr1 | hr1)
355     · refine Or.inl ⟨vsub_ne_zero.1 hp₁p₂, r⁻¹, ⟨(inv_pos.2 hr0).le, inv_le_one_of_one_le₀ hr1⟩, ?_⟩
356       rw [AffineMap.lineMap_apply, hp₃p₂, smul_smul, inv_mul_cancel₀ hr0.ne.symm, one_smul,
357         vsub_vadd]
358     · refine Or.inr ⟨?_, r, ⟨hr0.le, hr1.le⟩, ?_⟩
359       · rw [← @vsub_ne_zero V, hp₃p₂, smul_ne_zero_iff]
360         exact ⟨hr0.ne.symm, hp₁p₂⟩
361       · rw [AffineMap.lineMap_apply, ← hp₃p₂, vsub_vadd]
362   · rintro (⟨hp₁p₂, h⟩ | ⟨hp₃p₂, h⟩)
363     · exact h.angle₂₁₃_eq_zero_of_ne hp₁p₂
364     · exact h.angle₃₁₂_eq_zero_of_ne hp₃p₂
365 
366 /-- The angle between three points is zero if and only if one of the first and third points is
367 strictly between the other two, or those two points are equal but not equal to the second. -/
368 theorem angle_eq_zero_iff_eq_and_ne_or_sbtw {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} :
369     ∠ p₁ p₂ p₃ = 0 ↔ p₁ = p₃ ∧ p₁ ≠ p₂ ∨ Sbtw ℝ p₂ p₁ p₃ ∨ Sbtw ℝ p₂ p₃ p₁ := by
370   rw [angle_eq_zero_iff_ne_and_wbtw]
371   by_cases hp₁p₂ : p₁ = p₂; · simp [hp₁p₂]
372   by_cases hp₁p₃ : p₁ = p₃; · simp [hp₁p₃]
373   by_cases hp₃p₂ : p₃ = p₂; · simp [hp₃p₂]
374   simp [hp₁p₂, hp₁p₃, Ne.symm hp₁p₃, Sbtw, hp₃p₂]
375 
376 /-- An Unoriented angle is unchanged by replacing the third point by one strictly further away on
377 the same ray. -/
378 theorem _root_.Sbtw.angle_eq_right {p₂ p₃ p : P} (p₁ : P) (h : Sbtw ℝ p₂ p₃ p) :
379     ∠ p₁ p₂ p₃ = ∠ p₁ p₂ p :=
380   angle_eq_angle_of_angle_eq_pi _ h.angle₁₂₃_eq_pi
381 
382 /-- An Unoriented angle is unchanged by replacing the first point by one strictly further away on
383 the same ray. -/
384 theorem _root_.Sbtw.angle_eq_left {p₁ p p₂ : P} (p₃ : P) (h : Sbtw ℝ p₂ p₁ p) :
385     ∠ p₁ p₂ p₃ = ∠ p p₂ p₃ := by
386   simpa only [angle_comm] using h.angle_eq_right p₃
387 
388 /-- An Unoriented angle is unchanged by replacing the third point by one weakly further away on the
389 same ray. -/
390 theorem _root_.Wbtw.angle_eq_right {p₂ p₃ p : P} (p₁ : P) (h : Wbtw ℝ p₂ p₃ p) (hp₃p₂ : p₃ ≠ p₂) :
391     ∠ p₁ p₂ p₃ = ∠ p₁ p₂ p := by
392   by_cases hp₃p : p₃ = p; · simp [hp₃p]
393   exact Sbtw.angle_eq_right _ ⟨h, hp₃p₂, hp₃p⟩
394 
395 /-- An Unoriented angle is unchanged by replacing the first point by one weakly further away on the
396 same ray. -/
397 theorem _root_.Wbtw.angle_eq_left {p₁ p p₂ : P} (p₃ : P) (h : Wbtw ℝ p₂ p₁ p) (hp₁p₂ : p₁ ≠ p₂) :
398     ∠ p₁ p₂ p₃ = ∠ p p₂ p₃ := by
399   simpa only [angle_comm] using h.angle_eq_right p₃ hp₁p₂
400 
401 lemma angle_pointReflection_right {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} :
402     ∠ p₁ p₂ (AffineEquiv.pointReflection ℝ p₂ p₃) = π - ∠ p₁ p₂ p₃ := by
403   by_cases! h₃₂ : p₃ = p₂
404   · simp [h₃₂]
405     field
406   rw [eq_sub_iff_add_eq]
407   apply EuclideanGeometry.angle_add_angle_eq_pi_of_angle_eq_pi
408   exact Sbtw.angle₁₂₃_eq_pi <| (sbtw_pointReflection_of_ne ℝ h₃₂.symm).symm
409 
410 /-- Three points are collinear if and only if the first or third point equals the second or the
411 angle between them is 0 or π. -/
412 theorem collinear_iff_eq_or_eq_or_angle_eq_zero_or_angle_eq_pi {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} :
413     Collinear ℝ ({p₁, p₂, p₃} : Set P) ↔ p₁ = p₂ ∨ p₃ = p₂ ∨ ∠ p₁ p₂ p₃ = 0 ∨ ∠ p₁ p₂ p₃ = π := by
414   refine ⟨fun h => ?_, fun h => ?_⟩
415   · replace h := h.wbtw_or_wbtw_or_wbtw
416     by_cases h₁₂ : p₁ = p₂
417     · exact Or.inl h₁₂
418     by_cases h₃₂ : p₃ = p₂
419     · exact Or.inr (Or.inl h₃₂)
420     rw [or_iff_right h₁₂, or_iff_right h₃₂]
421     rcases h with (h | h | h)
422     · exact Or.inr (angle_eq_pi_iff_sbtw.2 ⟨h, Ne.symm h₁₂, Ne.symm h₃₂⟩)
423     · exact Or.inl (h.angle₃₁₂_eq_zero_of_ne h₃₂)
424     · exact Or.inl (h.angle₂₃₁_eq_zero_of_ne h₁₂)
425   · rcases h with (rfl | rfl | h | h)
426     · simpa using collinear_pair ℝ p₁ p₃
427     · simpa using collinear_pair ℝ p₁ p₃
428     · rw [angle_eq_zero_iff_ne_and_wbtw] at h
429       rcases h with (⟨-, h⟩ | ⟨-, h⟩)
430       · rw [Set.insert_comm]
431         exact h.collinear
432       · rw [Set.insert_comm, Set.pair_comm]
433         exact h.collinear
434     · rw [angle_eq_pi_iff_sbtw] at h
435       exact h.wbtw.collinear
436 
437 /-- If the angle between three points is 0, they are collinear. -/
438 theorem collinear_of_angle_eq_zero {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} (h : ∠ p₁ p₂ p₃ = 0) :
439     Collinear ℝ ({p₁, p₂, p₃} : Set P) :=
440   collinear_iff_eq_or_eq_or_angle_eq_zero_or_angle_eq_pi.2 <| Or.inr <| Or.inr <| Or.inl h
441 
442 /-- If the angle between three points is π, they are collinear. -/
443 theorem collinear_of_angle_eq_pi {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} (h : ∠ p₁ p₂ p₃ = π) :
444     Collinear ℝ ({p₁, p₂, p₃} : Set P) :=
445   collinear_iff_eq_or_eq_or_angle_eq_zero_or_angle_eq_pi.2 <| Or.inr <| Or.inr <| Or.inr h
446 
447 /-- If three points are not collinear, the angle between them is nonzero. -/
448 theorem angle_ne_zero_of_not_collinear {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} (h : ¬Collinear ℝ ({p₁, p₂, p₃} : Set P)) :
449     ∠ p₁ p₂ p₃ ≠ 0 :=
450   mt collinear_of_angle_eq_zero h
451 
452 /-- If three points are not collinear, the angle between them is not π. -/
453 theorem angle_ne_pi_of_not_collinear {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} (h : ¬Collinear ℝ ({p₁, p₂, p₃} : Set P)) :
454     ∠ p₁ p₂ p₃ ≠ π :=
455   mt collinear_of_angle_eq_pi h
456 
457 /-- If three points are not collinear, the angle between them is positive. -/
458 theorem angle_pos_of_not_collinear {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} (h : ¬Collinear ℝ ({p₁, p₂, p₃} : Set P)) :
459     0 < ∠ p₁ p₂ p₃ :=
460   (angle_nonneg _ _ _).lt_of_ne (angle_ne_zero_of_not_collinear h).symm
461 
462 /-- If three points are not collinear, the angle between them is less than π. -/
463 theorem angle_lt_pi_of_not_collinear {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} (h : ¬Collinear ℝ ({p₁, p₂, p₃} : Set P)) :
464     ∠ p₁ p₂ p₃ < π :=
465   (angle_le_pi _ _ _).lt_of_ne <| angle_ne_pi_of_not_collinear h
466 
467 /-- The cosine of the angle between three points is 1 if and only if the angle is 0. -/
468 nonrec theorem cos_eq_one_iff_angle_eq_zero {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} :
469     Real.cos (∠ p₁ p₂ p₃) = 1 ↔ ∠ p₁ p₂ p₃ = 0 :=
470   cos_eq_one_iff_angle_eq_zero
471 
472 /-- The cosine of the angle between three points is 0 if and only if the angle is π / 2. -/
473 nonrec theorem cos_eq_zero_iff_angle_eq_pi_div_two {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} :
474     Real.cos (∠ p₁ p₂ p₃) = 0 ↔ ∠ p₁ p₂ p₃ = π / 2 :=
475   cos_eq_zero_iff_angle_eq_pi_div_two
476 
477 /-- The cosine of the angle between three points is -1 if and only if the angle is π. -/
478 nonrec theorem cos_eq_neg_one_iff_angle_eq_pi {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} :
479     Real.cos (∠ p₁ p₂ p₃) = -1 ↔ ∠ p₁ p₂ p₃ = π :=
480   cos_eq_neg_one_iff_angle_eq_pi
481 
482 /-- The sine of the angle between three points is 0 if and only if the angle is 0 or π. -/
483 nonrec theorem sin_eq_zero_iff_angle_eq_zero_or_angle_eq_pi {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} :
484     Real.sin (∠ p₁ p₂ p₃) = 0 ↔ ∠ p₁ p₂ p₃ = 0 ∨ ∠ p₁ p₂ p₃ = π :=
485   sin_eq_zero_iff_angle_eq_zero_or_angle_eq_pi
486 
487 /-- The sine of the angle between three points is 1 if and only if the angle is π / 2. -/
488 nonrec theorem sin_eq_one_iff_angle_eq_pi_div_two {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} :
489     Real.sin (∠ p₁ p₂ p₃) = 1 ↔ ∠ p₁ p₂ p₃ = π / 2 :=
490   sin_eq_one_iff_angle_eq_pi_div_two
491 
492 /-- Three points are collinear if and only if the first or third point equals the second or
493 the sine of the angle between three points is zero. -/
494 theorem collinear_iff_eq_or_eq_or_sin_eq_zero {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} :
495     Collinear ℝ ({p₁, p₂, p₃} : Set P) ↔ p₁ = p₂ ∨ p₃ = p₂ ∨ Real.sin (∠ p₁ p₂ p₃) = 0 := by
496   rw [sin_eq_zero_iff_angle_eq_zero_or_angle_eq_pi,
497     collinear_iff_eq_or_eq_or_angle_eq_zero_or_angle_eq_pi]
498 
499 /-- If three points are not collinear, the sine of the angle between them is positive. -/
500 theorem sin_pos_of_not_collinear {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} (h : ¬Collinear ℝ ({p₁, p₂, p₃} : Set P)) :
501     0 < Real.sin (∠ p₁ p₂ p₃) :=
502   Real.sin_pos_of_pos_of_lt_pi (angle_pos_of_not_collinear h) (angle_lt_pi_of_not_collinear h)
503 
504 /-- If three points are not collinear, the sine of the angle between them is nonzero. -/
505 theorem sin_ne_zero_of_not_collinear {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} (h : ¬Collinear ℝ ({p₁, p₂, p₃} : Set P)) :
506     Real.sin (∠ p₁ p₂ p₃) ≠ 0 :=
507   ne_of_gt (sin_pos_of_not_collinear h)
508 
509 /-- If the sine of the angle between three points is 0, they are collinear. -/
510 theorem collinear_of_sin_eq_zero {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} (h : Real.sin (∠ p₁ p₂ p₃) = 0) :
511     Collinear ℝ ({p₁, p₂, p₃} : Set P) := by
512   revert h
513   contrapose
514   exact sin_ne_zero_of_not_collinear
515 
516 end EuclideanGeometry
